title: Adaptive lane coalescer for varlen requests with kernel-alignment and KV-cache awareness
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Mixed-length traffic produces inefficient GPU batches due to padding and kernel mismatch. This PR introduces an adaptive lane-based coalescer that groups concurrent requests into "lanes" based on sequence-length ranges and kernel alignment targets. The coalescer makes batching decisions that balance padding overhead, KV-cache locality, and kernel execution characteristics. Key ideas: 1) lane assignment uses a lightweight histogram maintained per-slot to pick lane bounds that align with the runtime's best-performing kernel sizes; 2) small lanes are opportunistically merged into adjacent lanes when kernel alignment and predicted padding cost indicate net win; 3) before merging, the coalescer evaluates KV-cache collision risk and prefers merges that preserve hot-cache entries to avoid cache thrash; 4) integrates with continuous batching: lanes are first-class scheduling units and can be flushed independently or coalesced by the slot scheduler based on pending volume and latency SLOs; 5) cost model uses profile data gathered by the kernel profiler (avg per-token kernel time by seqlen bucket) to estimate per-lane token cost and expected latency; 6) exposes two new runtime knobs: lane_target_utilization and kv_eviction_safety_margin, and a diagnostic endpoint (/debug/lane-coalescer) for live histograms and merge decisions. Implementation highlights: new coalescer and scheduler adaptor in serving/runtime/lanes, a lightweight in-memory histogram store, kernel-profile consumer hooks in serving/runtime/profiler, KV-cache-aware merge checks in serving/runtime/kv_cache_manager, and unit + integration tests for mixed workloads. Benchmarks: measured on a 8x A100 node with mixed GPT-like load (70% short <=64, 30% long <=1024) and steady QPS representative of production. Results: 12-18% P50 latency reduction across models tested, 22% reduction in wasted padding tokens (measured at the runtime batching boundary), and 8-11% lower end-to-end token cost for steady-state loads where KV-cache reuse is high. Compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via config flag lane_coalescer_enabled=false. Backwards-compatible when disabled. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime config and requires kernel profile data to be present for alignment benefits. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and cost model handwritten and linked in PR - [x] Unit tests for lane assignment and merge logic - [x] Integration test exercising KV-cache-aware merges - [x] Benchmarks and flamegraphs attached - [x] Docs entry for runtime knobs and diagnostic endpoint - [x] CI green and benchmarks validated in staging

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work. Please add a short explanation of the heuristic thresholds in the docs. How sensitive is lane_target_utilization to bursty traffic?
Aisha Patel: Added a paragraph in docs and added an autoscale-friendly mode that lowers merge aggressiveness under bursty conditions. See config sample in docs.
Rachel Lee: KV-cache awareness is critical. Two questions: 1) do we track per-model hot keys or per-slot? 2) how expensive is the cache-check on the hot path?
Aisha Patel: We track per-slot hot-key summaries (bloom filter + LRU counters) to keep the fast-path checks O(1). Expanded comments and tests to validate false-positive behavior.
Kenji Watanabe: CI had a flaky scheduling test on re-run. I suspect a race in slot flush; can you add a small jitter before forced flush in test?
Aisha Patel: Fixed test by introducing deterministic jitter and added a retry helper. Re-ran CI and benchmarks.
Rachel Lee: Approved after verifying benchmarks in staging and reviewing the diagnostic endpoint output.
Miguel Santos: Squash-merge ok after you address the one nit about log verbosity (reduce debug logs for production).
ci_details: Initial CI: 7/8 checks passed; flaky scheduling-test failed. After fix and small test changes CI: all checks passed. Lint: pass. Unit tests: pass. Integration staging run: pass. Benchmark job: pass (benchmarks uploaded to tools/benchmarks/lane_coalescer/bench_results.md).
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in lane-based coalescer that reduces padding waste and improves latency for mixed-length workloads. Exposes lane_target_utilization and kv_eviction_safety_margin runtime knobs and a diagnostic endpoint at /debug/lane-coalescer. Opt-in via runtime config lane_coalescer_enabled. Not enabled by default.
notes_for_ops: Staging rollout recommended. When enabling, ensure kernel-profile data is populated (runtime-profiling must have run for 24h or a minimum sample count). Watch /debug/lane-coalescer histograms and kv_eviction_metric. For high-burst traffic, use autoscale-friendly mode to reduce merge aggressiveness.
related_work: This draws on prior seqlen bucketing and pad-aware allocators but differs by making lanes first-class scheduling units tied to kernel alignment and KV-cache locality; see ENG-10205 for earlier pad allocator experiments.
